findings.reason: running §4 first either blocks on an unlanded §3 or forces §4 to duplicate §3's assembly, so the dependency that makes §3 the owner of G has to be declared.
findings.text: `s4` declares `depends-on: [iron-core-magnetisation#s2]`, but §4's mechanism solves F(M) = M − c(|B|)B with B = B_ext + G·M, and G is the cell interaction matrix §3 builds (the 3392-square matrix of §3's done-when (2)); the graph lets §4 be dispatched before the matrix it solves against exists

findings.reason: without a control, §3's only accuracy evidence is an agreement no wrong kernel would break; a control (a perturbed sheet sign or normal that must break the agreement) is what makes the measure able to fail.
findings.text: §3's done-when (1) compares the device build with "the §2 host route" but declares no negative control, and on the Part V strip branch both sides are the same polygon kernel (`_fill_tile` on the device, the §2 strip on the host), so the check passes vacuously for a wrong kernel

findings.reason: if the reference is only good to 1e-8 at half a cell width the node cannot distinguish a 1e-10 route from a failing one, so the criterion for the reference (refinement to a stated stability, or a second independent route) has to be named before the threshold means anything.
findings.text: §2 certifies 1e-10 against "a converged Gauss–Legendre integral" with no convergence criterion and no independent control, while the plan's own §1 evidence (lines 98–101) reports that this quadrature is near-singular for sliver cells and reads 4e-5 for the sphere's thin cells — the reference may be less accurate than the tolerance it is used to certify

findings.reason: the two changed sections now differ by 30× on the accuracy the chosen route can hold, and a worker that satisfies §2 will fail §3 on measurement noise; §3's tolerance has to come from §2's measured floor (or the comparison be taken at targets where the floor is lower).
findings.text: §2 states the strip's model error falls as ε² and the cancellation of its two long edges grows as the rounding error over ε, which puts the best attainable error at the crossing near ε ≈ 6 µm and ~3e-11 relative; §3's done-when (1) then demands the device build and the §2 host route agree to 1e-12 in float64, below that same roundoff floor, so the preferred Part V branch cannot meet §3 even when both sides are correct
